t.7.92.1: Hearing that, Rāghava, together with his brothers, was filled with joy, and Rāghava spoke to his brothers words that seemed wondrous.
t.7.92.2: O Saumitri, these two sons of yours, Aṅgada and Candraketu, are well versed in dharma, firm of bow, and worthy of kingship.
t.7.92.3: I will consecrate these two in kingship; let a region be properly chosen, one that is delightful and free from hostile neighbours, where the two bowmen may live happily.
t.7.92.4: O gentle one, let a land be found where there would be no harm to kings and no destruction of hermitages, so that we commit no offence.
t.7.92.5: When Rāma had spoken thus, Bharata replied: "This land, Kārāpatha, is very delightful and free from disease."
t.7.92.6: Let a city be founded there for the great-souled Aṅgada, and for Candraketu the lovely Candrakānta, free from all affliction.
t.7.92.7: Rāghava accepted those words spoken by Bharata, and having brought that country under his control, he settled it upon Aṅgada.
t.7.92.8: The city Aṅgadīyā, delightful and charming and well guarded, was established for Aṅgada by Rāma, whose deeds are accomplished without strain.
t.7.92.9: And for Candraketu, the wrestler, a city was founded in the land of the Mallas, renowned as Candrakāntā, divine like the city of heaven.
t.7.92.10: Then Rāma, Bharata and likewise Lakṣmaṇa, invincible in battle, attained the highest joy, and they performed the consecration.
t.7.92.11: Having consecrated the two princes and sent them forth with their armies and followers, Aṅgada to the western land and Candraketu facing the north,
t.7.92.13: Lakṣmaṇa, having then dwelt in Aṅgadīyā for a year, returned once more to Ayodhyā, his invincible son being firmly established there.
t.7.92.12: Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, followed Aṅgada, while Bharata became the guardian of Candraketu's rear.
t.7.92.14: Bharata too, having likewise stayed there for a year and somewhat more, returned to Ayodhyā and approached the feet of Rāma.
t.7.92.16: Thus ten thousand years passed for them then, as they ever strove in dharma and in the affairs of the citizens.
t.7.92.15: Both Saumitri and Bharata, exceedingly righteous and devoted to Rāma's feet, did not notice, out of their affection, even the time that had gone by.
t.7.92.17: Having passed their time in delight, their hearts wholly content, endowed with splendor and established on the supreme path of dharma, the three shone with blazing radiance like three fires well kindled and duly fed with oblations at a great sacrifice.
